# Recorded from a real AppleSMC on 2026-10-09, not generated.
#
#   machine: Mac16,9 (arm64), macOS 15.6
#   tool:    a standalone C probe driving IOKit. It re-declares SMCKeyData_t from
#            Apple's PowerManagement layout and asserts, in C, that the struct is
#            80 bytes with result at 40, data8 at 42, data32 at 44, bytes at 48.
#            No line below was produced by x's own code, so these bytes cannot
#            agree with a bug in it.
## Grammar (one record per line, parsed by the tests in src/common/smc.rs):
#   COUNT <n>                          the #KEY pseudo-key
#   KEY <name>                         the key at index i, one line per index, in
#                                      the order the SMC enumerated them. A key
#                                      with a non-printable byte prints as
#                                      `0x<hex8>` because only the value is
#                                      lossless.
#   DATA <name> <type_hex> <size> <payload_hex>
#                                      keyInfo's declared type and size plus the
#                                      payload, recorded for #KEY and for every
#                                      key the widened CPU filter accepts.
## This is a differentiated read of the full key set the CPU filter accepts: 132
# keys in five clusters (`Tp0*` 45, `Tp1*` 14, `Tp2*` 31, `Tpx*` 12, `Ts0*` 30),
# every cluster answering with its own spread — 45, 14, 31, 12 and 20 distinct
# values. Hottest is `Tp1o` at 82.109375 C (`0038a442` read as a little-endian
# single); the hottest `Tp0*` key in the same read is 78.265625 C, which is what
# x said while the filter only covered that one cluster.
